sections.html:
Three desks in the Bates County offices in Butler cover most property tax questions, and each has a room on West Dakota Street. The Collector/Treasurer is in Room 2 at 103 West Dakota, Butler, MO 64730. The Assessor is in Room 4, and the County Clerk is in Room 1. Courthouse offices keep 8:30 am to 4:30 pm hours on weekdays and close from noon to 1 pm.

Reach the Collector at 660-679-3341 or through the courthouse line at 660-386-7776, option 3. The Assessor answers at option 4 on the courthouse line. The Recorder of Deeds, in Room 3, handles the deed side of a sale. The Collector also acts as county Treasurer, so one office both collects the money and distributes it to schools, townships and the health center.

sections.h2: Selling a home in Bates County
sections.html:
Bates County is a rural part of west central Missouri, close to the Kansas line and part of the Kansas City metropolitan area. Butler is the county seat and largest city. The 2020 census counted 16,042 residents, with an estimate of 16,512 for 2025. The county had 7,189 housing units, 11.1% of them vacant, and 74.3% of occupied homes were owner occupied.

Several school districts reach into the county, including Butler R-V, Adrian R-III, Rich Hill R-IV and Drexel R-IV. Which district sits on your parcel affects the levy lines on the bill, so look at the statement itself.

sections.h2: When a Bates County tax bill turns delinquent
sections.html:
The cutoff is New Year's Day. RSMo 139.100 requires the collector to tack a penalty onto anything still open after January 1. A stamped envelope counts as paid on the postmark date, and registered or certified mail counts on its certification date. When a postmark is smudged or absent, the collector makes a judgment call and writes it down.

For 2026 bills, that makes December 31, 2026 the practical cutoff, with the new penalty arriving on January 1, 2027. The county has a 24-hour drop box on the east side of the Administration Building.

Bates County Collector payment rules

You can pay in person, by mail, online or through the drop box. Card fees are passed to the payer and none of that fee goes to Bates County, under RSMo 139.055.

  • In person at Room 2, 103 West Dakota, Butler.
  • By mail to the Collector's office, with a postmark on or before the deadline.
  • Online through the Collector's website, where debit cards cost $4.00 and credit cards cost 2.45%.
  • In the 24-hour drop box on the east side of the Administration Building.

A paid receipt shown on a phone screen works at the DMV or Department of Revenue office, so you don't need to wait for paper.

sections.h2: How the Bates County tax sale works
sections.html:
The Collector holds a delinquent real estate tax certificate sale on the fourth Monday of every August. The list of eligible parcels is published in July. To pull a parcel off the block, the full amount has to be in the office before 4:30 PM on the Friday ahead of the sale. Call the Collector for each year's exact dates and for how earlier sales turned out.

Payment on a sale-eligible parcel must be made by cash, money order, card or cashier's check. Web and phone payments are not allowed for those parcels.

Losing a parcel at auction isn't instant. RSMo 140.405 lets the owner buy it back, and the winning bidder has to mail a redemption notice, both first class and certified, at least ninety days before claiming a deed. An owner who wants to sell or borrow against the land has to redeem first, so ask the Collector for the redemption amount before you list a delinquent parcel.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Bates County assessment
sections.html:
Walk into Room 4 and ask the Assessor to look at your value again. Still unhappy? Take it to the local Board of Equalization. The County Clerk in Room 1 knows when the board sits and how to get on its calendar.

The next stop is the State Tax Commission under RSMo 138.430. Your complaint is due by September 30 of the assessment year or thirty days after the board rules, whichever comes later, and you attach the board's decision letter.

A home owned by a person or persons can appear without a lawyer. An LLC, trust, association or estate cannot. The Commission's phone number is 573-751-1715.

If you think the bill is wrong but don't want it going delinquent, RSMo 139.031 lets you pay it all and protest. File a written statement with the Collector giving your reasons and the value you claim. The undisputed share goes out to the taxing districts, and the disputed share sits in its own fund.

You then have ninety days to sue the Collector in circuit court. If a timely assessment appeal is already open at the State Tax Commission or a court, that appeal stands in for the suit.

Tax paid in error can be refunded on a written application filed within three years of payment.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or due
sections.html:
Ask for a payoff figure from the Collector's office before the contract date, and check the Collector's records for earlier years. Then give that number to the title company.

  • Confirm all current and delinquent real estate bills on the parcel.
  • Find out whether the parcel appears on a tax sale list.
  • Ask the Assessor about any pending change of value.
  • Confirm the Recorder in Room 3 will record the deed and release of any old deed of trust.

Unpaid tax follows the land, so a buyer takes the property subject to it. That is why title companies order a tax search early. A cash buyer will usually want the same search, but with no lender involved the payoff and recording steps can finish in a single visit once the Collector confirms a zero balance.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property taxes in Bates County, Missouri?
faqs.a: Pay the Bates County Collector in Room 2 at 103 West Dakota, Butler, by mail, online, or in the east side drop box of the Administration Building. Phone 660-679-3341. Card payments carry a fee passed to the payer.

faqs.q: When does a Bates County property tax bill become delinquent?
faqs.a: After December 31. Missouri law adds a penalty after January 1, and mailed payments count on their postmark date. Mail well before the cutoff so the postmark falls inside the window.

faqs.q: When is the Bates County tax sale?
faqs.a: The fourth Monday of August every year. Owners must pay in full at the office before 4:30 PM on the Friday before to stop the auction.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Bates County property value?
faqs.a: Start with the Assessor in Room 4, then use the Board of Equalization through the County Clerk. A further appeal goes to the Missouri State Tax Commission by September 30 or thirty days after the board's decision, whichever is later.

faqs.q: Can I pay my taxes under protest in Bates County?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay the whole bill before it turns delinquent and give the Collector a written statement of your grounds. A court action to recover the protested amount must follow within ninety days unless an assessment appeal is already pending.
